thread:
Sam (support): ACME reported streaming metrics flipping negative / zero during live sessions. TTFT shows -4.8s then 0 then normal. They want root cause and ETA. Screenshot attached: https://redwood-internal/screenshots/zz9a1

Sam (support): Happened ~2026-03-12T09:21Z on route /v1/stream. Customer on Hosted.

metrics-bot: ALERT negative_rate_detected route=\"/v1/stream\" env=prod count=5 window_start=2026-03-12T09:20:00Z

Priya (eng-platform): Can you paste a request id and the exact timestamp? Also confirm Hosted vs Dedicated.

Sam (support): req id rq_03d4f5b2 at 2026-03-12T09:21:03Z. Hosted. Customer says many user sessions hit alerts.

Ashok (eng-ml): Pulled raw events from clickhouse for rq_03d4f5b2. Looks like cumulative token counter goes down between adjacent rows which makes our delta negative. Sample rows:
```
req_id | ts                      | cumulative_tokens
rq_03d4f5b2 | 2026-03-12T09:21:00Z | 2048
rq_03d4f5b2 | 2026-03-12T09:21:01Z | 2039  <-- decreased
rq_03d4f5b2 | 2026-03-12T09:21:02Z | 2060
```

Jorge (eng-sre): Could be out-of-order writes or a duplicate/replay from the runtime during restart. Which component writes cumulative_tokens?

Ashok (eng-ml): Serving runtime emits per-chunk cumulative counters. There's a known transient restart case that can re-emit chunks. We had a kernel roll earlier today but not sure it's related.

Priya (eng-platform): Our Console computes rate with delta(cumulative)/delta(time). If cumulative decreases we currently render negative rate. Short-term we can clamp negatives to 0 in the dashboard query + add an annotation explaining the banner.

Sam (support): Customer wants a short-term fix to stop ops alerts, plus timeline for a permanent fix.

Ashok (eng-ml): I repro'd locally by simulating a stale resend: emit counters 1000 -> 1200 -> 1190 (stale) -> 1300 then run metric calc and see negative tokens/sec for that interval. Repro steps:
1) start streaming sim mode on local runtime
2) emit chunk counters: 1000, 1200, 1190, 1300
3) run the same aggregation query (lag over ts) to compute per-second rate

Priya (eng-platform): Proposed actions:
- immediate (<=2h): clamp negative rates to 0 in Console and annotate affected windows + incident banner
- short (24h): modify aggregation to treat cumulative as monotonic (ignore decreases) and filter out-of-order older events before delta
- long (48-72h): add sequence ids to runtime chunk events so ingest can drop stale resends

Jorge (eng-sre): I'll check kafka consumer logs for replays and offsets to see if the runtime replayed a batch.

Sam (support): Customer replied: \"Appreciate the quick patch. Please give us a timeline for the permanent fix so we can plan our alerts.\"

Priya (eng-platform): I'll PR the dashboard clamp (GREATEST(rate, 0)) to canary. Will add an annotation at 2026-03-12T09:20:00Z.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy dashboards/metrics-clamp v1.2.3 -> success (canary=10%)

Ashok (eng-ml): I'll open INF-4721 to track ingest transform changes + runtime sequence ids. Target: implement and test within 48h.

Jorge (eng-sre): Found a restart on runtime-09 at 08:59 UTC with a short window of reprocessed offsets around 09:21:00. Looks like replayed batch triggered stale counters.

Priya (eng-platform): Canary patched. Monitoring dashboards. If stable we'll roll to 100% in ~30m. Also adding incident note to #incidents.

deploy-bot: rollout complete dashboards/metrics-clamp v1.2.3 -> success (100%)

Sam (support): Customer confirms they now see 0 instead of negative values and alerts stopped. Asked for postmortem and INF-4721 link.

Ashok (eng-ml): Implementing monotonic counter in ingest transform now, ETA 24h for rollout to prod testing. Runtime change to attach sequence id ETA ~72h with staged rollout.

Jorge (eng-sre): Added a short debounce on runtime restart path to reduce immediate replay risk. Monitoring for next 24h.

Priya (eng-platform): Closing escalation with customer: dashboard clamp deployed, root cause likely duplicate/out-of-order chunk events from transient runtime restart, tracking INF-4721 for permanent fixes. Will post final incident note after INF-4721 merges.

Sam (support): Customer acknowledged and closed. Thanks team :thumbsup:
